segments: The eighteenth dynasty.
The Emperors of the Romans.
A comet appeared in the sky,
and many were saying that his end was near, on account of the signs that were numerous.
And while that emperor Theodosius, on a certain day, was riding a horse as usual in the royal city and going out to the campus (or field) as if for recreation,
the horse stumbled and fell.
And the vertebra {OCR?} of his neck was crushed,
and they brought him in on a litter.
And when he saw that his end was near, he summoned Pulcheria, his sister,
and informed her that Marcian would reign after him.
And he also summoned Marcian and commanded him
to conduct the affairs of the state in the fear of God.
And after two days he passed away.
After Theodosius the Younger {OCR?}, [Marcian reigned] seven years.
This man took as a wife Pulcheria, the sister of the emperor Theodosius,
she who had supposedly lived an ascetic monastic life the whole time of her brother.
She was, however, suspected of having had relations with Marcian,
which indeed openly became his wife after the death of Theodosius.
And because, under an affected and false appearance, she was not consenting to belong to a man and break her ascetic vow,
certain bishops, who were respecters of persons and inclined toward the duality of natures, persuaded her to consent,
and [promised] that they would impose upon the entire people
that for one week in the year they should abstain from meat on her behalf,
and eat monastic food.
Then she was persuaded,
and broke her vow,
and stripped off her monastic habit.
And within two years she convened a council at Chalcedon,

which, along with the confession of the duality of natures, also decreed the abstinence of the week before the Dominical Fast upon those who accepted it. But when the Orthodox Egyptians in Egypt saw the Dyophysites boasting over them because of their abstinence from meat during that week,
they [abstained] not only from meat,
but also from all carnal superfluities.
[Editorial note by Bedjan:] ... he wronged the bishops of the Catholic faith and Saint Pulcheria with the slanders that he found in the books of the members of his sect.
Because he was a Jacobite,
he continually calls the members of his faction 'Orthodox',
and the members of the true Church 'Chalcedonians'.
This warning suffices for this entire history.
